verdict.line: You lose if K'Sante catches a charged W (Path Maker) stun on you near a wall and chains it into R (All Out) before you have Black Cleaver; you win if you bait out his E (Footwork) and land an empowered W (Ruthless Predator) to strip his shield and stun-lock him.

brief.thesis: The matchup is even on paper (49.7% baseline) but Renekton actually wins the head-to-head at 52.6% over 2086 games because his empowered W (Ruthless Predator) deletes K'Sante's Footwork shield the instant it lands, and E (Slice and Dice)'s armor shred compounds with Black Cleaver to out-damage K'Sante's duel kit by mid-game. K'Sante still owns the solo-kill column: his R (All Out) knocks you through walls and then goes All Out with bonus healing and damage at the cost of his own defenses, so any all-in he starts near a wall before you have items is his fight, not yours.

theirWindow.when: charged W (Path Maker) stun lands near a wall
theirWindow.what: Path Maker's knockback can launch you through terrain, and from level 6 he can follow with R (All Out) to dash after you with bonus damage and healing at reduced defenses. Don't greed trades with your back near a wall once he's level 6 and R is up.

yourWindow.what: Footwork is his only shield and escape dash, on an 8-10s cooldown that drops as he levels it. The moment it's spent, he has no shield to eat your burst and no dash to disengage — step in with empowered W (Ruthless Predator) once you're above 50 Fury to strip any shield and stun him for 1.5s, then follow with E (Slice and Dice) and Q (Cull the Meek).

start.why: 52.2% win rate over 1844 games and the 76.7% pick — the sustain and early AD help you win the Q (Cull the Meek) sustain trades before his Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks matter.

boots.why: 53.2% win rate over 1603 games and the 73% pick — K'Sante's passive marks your attacks and his autos add up over a long lane; flat auto-attack reduction blunts that more than magic resist does.

core.why: Highest-performing order at 66.4% win rate (113 games) when built first — the armor shred stacks on top of your own E (Slice and Dice) shred, making empowered W (Ruthless Predator) hit even harder once his Footwork shield is gone.
Part of the top three build paths (13%, 10.6%, 9.1% pick combined) — the shield proc covers you through his charged W (Path Maker) and rewards the all-in you're setting up with Fury.
Appears in both top win-rate paths (51.6% and 66.4%) — the damage-over-time conversion keeps you alive through his R (All Out) burst window when his own defenses are down.

situational.when: he's building toward all-inning you with R (All Out) and you need the health and tenacity to survive the knockback-stun chain
the lane is stable and you want faster W (Ruthless Predator) and E (Slice and Dice) cooldowns to punish his Footwork downtime more often
he's kiting with E (Footwork) speed and you need the slow to stick empowered W (Ruthless Predator)

runes.keystoneWhy: Extended trades are where Renekton wins this matchup — Conqueror's healing scales with the longer fights your Q (Cull the Meek) sustain and Fury stacking are built to create.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite runs a 52% win rate at 70.4% pick rate — Ignite denies the healing his E (Footwork) and R (All Out) grant him, which is exactly the sustain that keeps this an even lane instead of a win.

playing.title: Track his Q stack count
playing.detail: Ntofo Strikes (Q) grants a stack on hit and fires a pulling shockwave at 2 stacks. Don't stand in range after he's already landed one Q — the second one yanks you in for free damage.

playing.title: Save empowered W for his Footwork
playing.detail: Above 50 Fury, W (Ruthless Predator) becomes three slashes that destroy damage shields outright. Holding it until after he's shielded with E (Footwork) turns your stun into a shield-break instead of wasted damage.

playing.title: Respect walls after level 6
playing.detail: His R (All Out) knocks you back through any wall behind you, then he dashes in All Out with bonus damage and healing at reduced defenses. Fight with your back to open space, not terrain, once he hits 6.

playing.title: Trade on his E cooldown, not yours
playing.detail: Footwork (E) is his only disengage and only shield, sitting at 8-10s depending on rank. Initiate your W into E combo in the window right after he's spent it, not on cooldown parity with your own E (Slice and Dice).

playing.title: Use E to poke, not just engage
playing.detail: Slice and Dice (E) reduces armor on everything it hits when empowered. Dashing through him early in a trade sets up every follow-up auto and ability for more damage, even if you don't fully commit.

playing.title: Hold R for the shred window, not the engage
playing.detail: Dominus (R) just transforms and pulses damage around you — it isn't a gap closer like his. Pop it after you're already in range with E (Slice and Dice) so the Fury generation and bonus health carry you through his counter-burst.

playing.title: Don't force all-ins before 3 items
playing.detail: Solo-kill advantage sits with K'Sante through the early-mid game because his R (All Out) burst window is safer than your transform. Wait until Black Cleaver and Eclipse are online before you commit to a kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the power-curve timing and trade-pattern reasoning connecting them to specific ability cooldowns and mechanics is my own tactical read, not sourced data.
